title: Voyager 1 is now one light-day from Earth

post.youtube_title: Voyager 1 Is Now One Light-Day From Earth 🛰️ #shorts
post.caption: Launched in 1977 with 69 KB of memory, Voyager 1 just became the first human-made object one full light-day from Earth. A signal now takes 24 hours to reach it 🤯
post.pinned_comment: If you could add one thing to the Golden Record, what would it be? 👇

sources: NASA/JPL: Voyager 1 reaches one light-day (about 25.9 billion km) from Earth on November 18, 2026
NASA/JPL: Voyager 1 entered interstellar space in August 2012; speed about 61,000 km/h relative to the Sun
NASA/JPL: Pale Blue Dot, taken February 14, 1990, from about 6 billion km; Earth spans less than a pixel
Voyager computers: about 69.6 KB of memory in total (CCS, FDS and AACS)

beats.text: A radio signal sent to {Voyager 1|Voyager one} now takes a *full* *day* to get there.
On November 18th, {2026|twenty twenty-six}, it becomes the first human-made object to reach one *light-day* from Earth. That's nearly 26 billion kilometers away.
It launched in 1977, the same year the very first *Star* *Wars* movie came out.
And it still runs on computers with about *69* kilobytes of memory. That's less than a single photo on your phone.
In 1990, from about six billion kilometers away, it turned around and took this picture.
That tiny speck is *Earth*. Every human who ever lived, on less than a single pixel.

beats.text: In 2012, {Voyager 1|Voyager one} left the Sun's bubble of solar wind, and entered *interstellar* space.
It's flying at about 61,000 kilometers per hour, and it's never coming back.
Its nuclear power is fading, and one day soon, it will fall silent.
But it will keep drifting between the stars for billions of years, carrying a *golden* *record* of sounds and pictures from Earth.
If you could add one thing to that record, what would it be?
